q: The rate of doing work is defined as ____.
e: Power is work per unit time. In SI that unit is the watt: 1 W = 1 J s⁻¹. The rate of doing work is defined as power.

q: The unit for power in SI units is the ____.
e: SI power is the watt. Erg per second is CGS. Horsepower is the British engineering unit. The unit for power in SI units is the watt (W).

q: If the work done is 1 joule in 1 second, the power is ____.
e: One joule in one second is one watt. If the work done is 1 joule in 1 second, the power is 1 watt.

q: The units of power which are larger than watt are kilowatt (kW) and ____.
e: 1 kW = 10³ W and 1 MW = 10⁶ W. The units of power which are larger than watt are kilowatt (kW) and megawatt (MW). Megawatt (mw) is what this sentence is naming.
1 kW = 1000 W, 1 MW = 10⁶ W, and 1 hp = 746 W = 550 ft-lb s⁻¹. 1 kW = 10³ W.
1 kW = 1000 W, 1 MW = 10⁶ W, and 1 hp = 746 W = 550 ft-lb s⁻¹. 1 MW = 10^6 W.

q: In the CGS system, the unit of power is ____.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. In the CGS system, the unit of power is erg s^-1.

q: In the British system, the unit of power is ____.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. In the British system, the unit of power is foot-pound per second (ft-lb s^-1).

q: In British engineering system, the unit of power is ____.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. In British engineering system, the unit of power is horse power (hp).

q: If the work done in 1 second is 550 ft-lb, the power is ____.
e: 550 ft-lb in one second is one horsepower. If the work done in 1 second is 550 ft-lb, the power is 1 horse power.
CGS power is the erg per second. 1 W = 10^7 erg s^-1.
1 kW = 1000 W, 1 MW = 10⁶ W, and 1 hp = 746 W = 550 ft-lb s⁻¹. 1 hp = 746 W.
CGS power is the erg per second. 1 hp = 746 × 10^7 erg s^-1.

q: For uniform motion, $P = Fv$ where $v$ is ____.
e: At constant speed, power is force times velocity, P = Fv. For uniform motion, P = Fv where v is average velocity.

q: Power is not a fundamental concept like energy but it is a very important concept for ____.
e: The fundamental is the lowest standing-wave frequency. Higher ones are harmonics or overtones. Power is not a fundamental concept like energy but it is a very important concept for engineering works.

q: Car engines, water pumps, refrigerators, air conditioners and electric bulbs, etc., are specified according to their ____.
e: Machines are rated by the power they consume or deliver. Car engines, water pumps, refrigerators, air conditioners and electric bulbs, etc., are specified according to their power consumption.
